raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #62705. Propagate DiffusionGemma image-prefix ranges into MRV2 attention metadata and apply vision bidirectional masking only to sliding layers.

## Claims

- Image prefill uses the configured vision mask with FA4 and Triton; full layers retain causal prompt attention.
- FA4 preserves per-request causal/noncausal mask semantics when image prefill shares a batch with denoising.
- Uniform denoise/commit FULL graphs remain supported. Prefill/mixed batches use eager or piecewise execution to avoid freezing optional image-range arguments into generic FULL graphs.

## Validation

Original submitted revision (`41fc44ca4728`), H100 PCIe 80 GiB, TP1. The submitter reviewed every changed line and independently reran the following focused command, reporting the same **56 passed, 10 skipped** as the agent run:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 ../.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py tests/v1/sample/test_diffusion_gemma_reads.py -q -rs
```

The numerical regression fails on the unmodified baseline: 27,764/148,480 elements differ, maximum absolute error 0.4235759 (atol=rtol=0.02). Propagating ranges alone also fails because FA4 previously excluded tensor causal flags from mm-prefix masking. Tests exercise actual ModelState metadata, paged-cache attention, model forward mask clearing, and CUDA graph replay. Three additional attention comparisons against the real Transformers Gemma4 vision-mask helper passed. Scoped pre-commit, including mypy, passed.

[Validation report, raw scores, dataset manifest, reproduction scripts, logs, and checkpoint hashes](https://gist.github.com/MuonChaser/b4f76755cf3697182682a9d960e33f31).

Agent-run pretrained evaluation: `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` at `f7f5b7f5fa82ffc52addd066915886d497f5517b`, all 11 shard hashes verified; BF16, FA4, MRV2. A-OKVQA validation, first 75 records sorted by question ID, one run per arm. Both primary arms use eager execution and identical deterministic answer canvases. Native chat endpoint, one denoising step, four letter logprobs from unconstrained vocabulary logits: **forced-choice reads**, not free generation.

| Check | Baseline | Patch |
|---|---:|---:|
| Image reads | 59/75 | 62/75 |
| Isolated text controls | 5/15 | 5/15; identical label logprobs |
| Patched FULL-decode vs patched eager | — | All 56 requests identical in answers and four label logprobs |

Six primary image answers changed: four incorrect-to-correct, one correct-to-incorrect, one incorrect-to-different-incorrect. All **288 HTTP requests** succeeded, including warm prefixes, later-chunk images, and concurrent image/text reads. Actual mixed vision-prefill/denoise batches were observed, with ranges only on sliding layers. The FULL control downgraded to FULL_DECODE_ONLY and captured uniform decode graphs.

<details>
<summary>Evaluation limits and environment</summary>

- Letter probability mass is often low (median 0.02459 baseline, 0.02896 patch). This small one-step evaluation does not establish general quality or statistical significance.
- Exact warm/cold and concurrent/single numerical parity is not established. Maximum warm/cold label-logprob deltas: 2.0891 baseline, 2.4263 patch; answer changes 1/15 and 0/15. Concurrent/single answer changes: 0/8 baseline, 2/8 patch (one image and one text, both incorrect-to-correct). Raw deltas are included; no batch-invariance claim is made.
- Supplemental agent-run controls: **336 HTTP requests**, three repetitions of individual/text-only/mixed modes with fixed canvases and isolated cold/warm cache namespaces. The original text probe also flips B→D in unmodified baseline text-only cold-cache batches in all three repetitions. Across arms, all 48 individual text requests have identical scores; all 48 text-batch answers agree, while logprobs still vary. Mixed text answers differ 3/24. Online microbatch layouts differ, so this is not a proof of batch invariance or a complete root-cause diagnosis.
- A separate **16-request diagnostic** compares the new image-range route with the original dynamic-causal route on identical real model Q/K/V and KV cache, checking only text-only rows. All **100 layer/request comparisons** (20,992,000 elements; 50 denoise rows) pass `atol=rtol=0.02`; maximum absolute difference is 0.0625, so outputs are not bitwise identical. Diagnostic GPU launches/host reads are outside production code and excluded from batch-variance measurements. Full scripts/raw results are in `supplemental-batch-validation.md` in the linked artifact.
- Both arms use identical compatible native artifacts/generated CuTe sources from wheel `0.32.1rc1.dev3+g3c1365373` with base `f1dbfef799`/patch Python source, Torch 2.14.0+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, Triton 3.8.0. This was not a fresh native build.
- CI exercises the existing attention suite on H100/B200. The 10 skips here are six Blackwell FlashInfer cases and four reverse-child/FP8 variants. Model A/B was performed outside CI. Full-suite, ROCm, TP>1, Blackwell, long free generation, default-O2 performance, and full Transformers DiffusionGemma output parity were not validated.

</details>

### Explicit FULL graph performance tradeoff (agent-run)

[Performance report, reproduction scripts, per-run metrics, per-request latencies, and runtime configuration evidence](https://gist.github.com/MuonChaser/78a9b1af1a33e81865b0a1f80658dba2).

Same H100 PCIe 80 GiB, TP1, BF16/FA4, fixed 16 GiB KV cache (75,989 tokens in every boot), prefix caching off. Explicit `FULL`, Torch compile mode 0: baseline runs FULL prefill/decode; patch runs NONE prefill and FULL uniform decode. Text requests use the **MM-enabled engine**. Warmed image processing, synthetic padding to exactly 512/2,048 prompt tokens, fixed 32-position canvas, one denoising step. Closed-loop concurrency 1/8; three repetitions per case. Latency is nonstreaming end-to-end, not TTFT/TPOT. All **20,736 timed + 1,920 warmup requests** succeeded with the expected token counts. No diagnostic hooks were enabled.

Median req/s in the initial matrix (latency is the corresponding mean E2E):

| Input | Prompt tokens | Concurrency | Baseline FULL | Patch FULL-decode | Throughput change | Mean E2E ms, base → patch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Image | 512 | 1 | 12.83 | 9.35 | −27.1% | 77.9 → 106.9 |
| Text | 512 | 1 | 16.61 | 12.25 | −26.3% | 60.2 → 81.7 |
| Image | 512 | 8 | 30.59 | 30.16 | −1.4% | 258.8 → 264.6 |
| Text | 512 | 8 | 45.26 | 34.86 | −23.0% | 174.2 → 228.7 |
| Image | 2,048 | 1 | 7.73 | 7.71 | −0.3% | 129.3 → 129.6 |
| Text | 2,048 | 1 | 8.87 | 9.46 | +6.6% | 112.7 → 105.7 |
| Image | 2,048 | 8 | 13.20 | 12.67 | −4.0% | 588.5 → 615.7 |
| Text | 2,048 | 8 | 13.45 | 13.28 | −1.3% | 579.3 → 587.7 |

Fresh reverse-order boots and longer concurrency-8 windows confirm a material short-prompt concurrency-1 cost: **text −27.7%, image −29.4%**. Text concurrency-8 medians fall 22.4% in this recheck, but baseline ranges are wide and overlap the patch; image concurrency-8 changes sign to +3.0%, also with wide overlapping ranges. All original runs, including outliers, are retained. The host was shared and GPU clocks were unlocked; these are bounded observations, not an isolated high-concurrency cost estimate or a general speedup claim.

Eager controls show smaller 512-token/concurrency-1 patch differences (text −2.8%, image −5.7%). They provide context, not an additive decomposition: baseline image attention is incorrect/causal, and the patch changes masking and potentially MoE routing. Repeated padded prompts and one-step reads do not represent long free generation or cold image ingestion. Both arms reuse the same native artifacts described above. **Default O2 uses FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, with ordinary prefill already piecewise; default-O2 performance was not measured.** The explicit-FULL regression is a correctness/performance tradeoff for review; this PR does not recover FULL prefill graph coverage.

### Rebase compatibility validation (2026-10-24)

Rebased onto `c50aca14416e`; compatibility source `b1a76d1a033b`. Preserved both documentation notes and adapted to the unified range helper from merged #56937, with test type narrowing. No attention-math or graph-policy change. In a rebuilt independent H100 environment, the full focused suite passed **56 tests, 10 skipped (145.96 s)**, plus **3 real HF Gemma4 mask comparisons**. Scoped pre-commit/mypy passed. [Rebase report, raw passing/setup-failure logs, source hashes and environment/configuration manifests](https://gist.github.com/MuonChaser/b4f76755cf3697182682a9d960e33f31#file-rebase-20261024-report-md).

Core versions/native artifacts match the original validation; this is not a fresh native build. The ten skips retain the existing Blackwell/reverse-child/FP8 reasons. Two earlier attempts failed solely on missing offline configuration metadata; both logs are retained, with no code/tolerance/skip changes between attempts. Original pretrained A/B and throughput results above remain measurements on `41fc44ca4728`, not the rebased source. The submitter confirmed the compatibility-diff review and personal test recheck before this update.

## Details

DiffusionGemma overrides `ModelState.prepare_attn` without forwarding `mm_req_doc_ranges`. It also uses per-request causal tensors, which FA4's mm-prefix path previously excluded. The fix reuses `compute_mm_prefix_ranges`, supplies the CPU sequence-length bound, slices active request offsets, and reuses Gemma4's full-layer range clearing. FA4's existing CuTe mask factory accepts persistent per-request causal flags without GPU host reads.

Generic FULL prefill/mixed graph coverage is reduced on an MM-prefix engine, including for its text requests; uniform denoise/commit graphs remain. Language-only engines retain existing support. No throughput improvement is claimed. Strict sync diagnostics fail on both baseline and patch at the unchanged sampler `if just_converged.any()`; no suppression or sampler change is included.

Duplicate checks refreshed before submission: #62437 is merged frontend joint/image reads; #49202 addresses denoise rectangular SWA; #62516 adds Blackwell FlashInfer mixed-causal support. #50539 changes oversized-range filtering and #56813 caches default-state ranges; neither propagates ranges from DiffusionGemma's custom state. Newer #63033/#63044 fix PaliGemma whole-prompt prefix attention; neither changes DiffusionGemma custom-state range propagation. No frontend, scheduler, native kernel, or denoise rectangular-SWA change is included here.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to implement and validate this change and prepare this description. Human review and personal focused-test execution were confirmed before submission.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>
